title: Adaptively-refinable polar-spline discrete differential forms: hierarchical construction, exactness, and applications
summary: A common approach to representing disk-like and sphere-like geometries in isogeometric analysis is to use collapsed-edge singularities in the underlying parameterization. The resulting tensor-product B-spline spaces on such singular parameterizations lack the required smoothness to be used in isogeometric analysis. Polar splines (Toshniwal et al., CMAME 2017) rectify this issue by extracting a smoother subspace, and have been successfully used to discretize high-order partial differential equations, as well as to perform structure-preserving discretizations of the de Rham complex.The latter…
